source: Plants make their own food (a sugar) in their leaves from sunlight, water and carbon dioxide from the air. They give off oxygen. Roots take in water; they do not "eat" soil.
Thinking plants get their food from the soil. The soil gives water and a few minerals; most of a plant's mass comes from air and water.
You eat to get food. A tree never eats a thing, yet it grows huge. Where does its food come from?

Plants make their own food in their leaves. They use sunlight for energy, water from their roots and carbon dioxide, a gas in the air. They make a sugar for food and give off oxygen. This is called photosynthesis.
Sunlight, water and carbon dioxide go in; sugar is made and oxygen comes out.

Most of a tree's wood is built from carbon dioxide taken out of the air and water from the ground. The soil gives only a few minerals. Scientists weighed soil before and after growing a tree in it and found the soil had lost almost nothing.
A plant is kept in a dark closet for two weeks with water. What happens?
It turns pale and weak, and it may die.
Without light, it cannot make food.
Thinking plants get their food from the soil. Soil gives water and minerals, but the food is made in the leaves.
